edition.name: 'Thoughts of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus', translated and edited by George Long (1862), Project Gutenberg eBook #15877, released 22 May 2005, transcribed by the Online Distributed Proofreading Team
edition.status: The translation carries its own copyright, so the translator's death year decides the UK and EU term. Long died 1879. The file's header names Long as translator and editor. It opens with a biographical sketch and an essay on the philosophy of Antoninus, both in Long's voice, then the twelve books with Long's footnotes, then an index of terms. No introduction by another hand appears in the file. The workbook draws on the twelve books only. The file does not name the printing it was transcribed from (publisher and year are not stated). It is an illustrated edition in American spelling, which suggests a later American printing of Long's text, so the printing is [to confirm]. The Gregory Hays and Robin Hard translations are in copyright and are not used.

tierNote: Research 4 Tier A: published before 1931 and every author and translator died before 1946 (docs/planning/AK_Demo_Catalogue_Plan.md section 7).

modernisation.rulesApplied: Reversible rules only (MODERNISATION_RULES in packages/validate/src/classics.ts). Spelling and typography, nothing that changes a word's meaning.
modernisation.revertChecked: Reverting the log on the modernised text returns the cut source byte for byte.
modernisation.knownIssue: The double-hyphen rule writes a comma and a space. Where the printed text had a comma before the dash, the result is a doubled comma. There are 39 in the twelve books. No quotation in the workbook includes one. A tooling fix (consume the preceding comma) is a separate commit.
modernisation.outsideTheRules: Long's American spellings (labor, honor, favor) are not covered by the rules and stay as printed inside quotations. The workbook's own prose is en-GB.
modernisation.editorial: No [Editorial] changes were made. Quotations are exact, checked by book and section against the modernised copy.
